boundaries.reason: The source-bound scalar budget/read-length, finite ASCII metadata, and bounded actual std::path proofs do not establish native Git configuration and path output, canonical directory identity and case folding, declaration stability, ignore matching, concurrent mutation, capability-relative file opening, Windows reparse semantics, or tar publication. The actual source adapter captures canonical Git/common directories through individually bounded queries before top-level discovery, refuses selected metadata/bare roots or unresolved declarations, and excludes both trees after canonicalization from the merged tracked and walker paths. Git's bounded untracked-path query owns Git-ignore precedence; the walker retains .ignore and no-follow entry policy. One retained selected-root capability owns archive admission.
boundaries.evidence: Native source, source_archive, source_fingerprint and source_file tests cover Git-written global excludes paths with spaces and inherited config-count context, ignored tracked modified bytes, ignored untracked exclusion, deletion, real .GIT metadata, and subdirectory paths. Actual Git oracle fixtures cover ancestor-ignored exclusion, competing relative excludes files, repository-root anchored patterns, and separate-directory info/exclude precedence with .gitignore negation. Separate, distinct common, forced-tracked metadata and nested-selection controls require only current working bytes; malformed ancestor declarations, selected metadata/bare roots, and unresolved case aliases refuse, while valid symlink/case aliases are bound to actual canonical directories and non-Git HEAD/objects working names remain ordinary input. Finite Miri controls bind Path::components to the actual typed matcher for whole components and rooted/relative namespaces. Shared runtime/build readers retain every captured parent; Unix uses public cap-primitives open_dir_nofollow and safe rustix NOFOLLOW|NONBLOCK|CLOEXEC, while Windows NtCreateFile uses RootDirectory and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT for every component, rejecting non-disk/reparse handles before reads. Native controls replace inspected parents/final files, rename captured ancestors/root names, refuse a writerless FIFO within a killed/reaped child deadline, preserve read errors, and bound growth/truncation reads to admitted length+1. Native parser tests admit exactly MAX_PATH_BYTES in complete valid records and refuse one extra path byte separately from stream/count/record limits. Native case folding, custom bare identification without Git or an explicit declaration, and one atomic view of concurrently modified Git state/files are not claimed.
boundaries.reconsider: Git output, ancestor ignore semantics, or capability/filesystem semantics change, a native source, link, budget, collision or archive contract fails, or a verifier can check the actual Git/filesystem adapter boundary.

boundaries.reason: The bounded Write-port proof does not establish native Unix socket EOF, launchd, descriptor inheritance, concurrency, or every possible Write implementation.
boundaries.evidence: The mandatory Mac workspace test gate exercises actual readiness and refusal through UnixStream while another receiver handle remains open; the cross-platform login_reply target checks partial, interrupted, empty, zero, and failed writes plus shutdown failures, and its finite Miri lane imports the same production adapter.
boundaries.reconsider: Reply framing or socket semantics change, a native integration fails, or a verifier supports the actual concurrent operating-system boundary.

boundaries.reason: The finite protocol step and job-state proofs do not establish filesystem locking, worker creation, SSH reliability, or native process lifetime.
boundaries.evidence: Native workspace tests exercise duplicate and conflicting submission, the existing launch-lock boundary, finished-job retries, launch refusal, and missing-supervisor state through the production app and Store adapters.
boundaries.reconsider: The launch or store locking protocol changes, a native adapter contract fails, or a verifier supports the actual filesystem and process boundary.

boundaries.reason: The supported native Kani, Quint/Apalache, Miri, and libFuzzer owner lane runs on Linux and Mac; native Windows verifier capability is not claimed.
boundaries.evidence: Linux or Mac: mise run verify and mise run miri on the exact source digest; Windows: cargo xtask verify inventory, cargo xtask windows-contracts, and mise run test for native SDK, process ownership, and filesystem contracts.
boundaries.reconsider: A pinned native verifier supports Windows, the implementation adds target-specific core decisions, or any native Windows contract fails.

boundaries.reason: Kani does not establish concurrent Win32 kernel ownership or foreign-function behavior.
boundaries.evidence: mise x -- cargo xtask windows-contracts; mise run test on Windows exercises capability, child ownership, failure cleanup, and process-tree termination.
boundaries.reconsider: A verifier supports the actual Win32 boundary, SDK semantics change, or a native ownership contract fails.
